item.title: Akita Inu: Meet Japan's National Dog — Odate, Akita Guide
item.description: The Akita is Japan’s most famous dog breed — designated a national natural monument in 1931 — and Odate City is its birthplace. The Akita Dog Museum (Akitainu Kaikan) lets visitors meet and pet purebred Akita Inu and learn the breed’s history, including the legendary loyal dog Hachiko, who was born nearby. Breeding farms offer guided meet-and-greets, and the city celebrates its dogs at an August festival. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Odate, Akita Hours Museum ~9:00–17:00 Admission Around ¥500–800 Time needed About 1 hour Best time Year-round; festival August What to Do Meet and pet purebred Akita Inu dogs.

item.title: Shibuya Guide: The Scramble Crossing & Shibuya Sky from Above
item.description: The Shibuya Scramble Crossing is the image that says “Tokyo” more than any other. When the lights turn red in every direction at once, up to 3,000 people surge across from all sides simultaneously beneath a blaze of giant video screens and neon — and somehow nobody collides. It happens again every couple of minutes, all day and late into the night. Watching it, and crossing it yourself, is a rite of passage on any first visit to the city.
